vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks when resolving static resources. An application can be vulnerable when it uses Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux, serves static resources from the file system, and has configured versioned resources support. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither file-system static resources nor versioned resource support is configured in any shipped component.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which does not configure the versioned file-system resource handling the advisory requires.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory requires an application that serves static resources from the file system and has versioned resource support configured. The application configures neither: it packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources static-location or resource-chain properties, and none of its own classes references VersionResourceResolver, ResourceChainRegistration or a resource-handler registry. Spring Boot registers versioned resource resolution only when the resource-chain strategy properties are set.

vulnerabilities.description: Due to incorrect escaping, the use of JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape() may lead to JavaScript code injection in the browser, potentially resulting in a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped code calls JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape().

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, and in it the only callers of the faulty escape are JSP tags that are never loaded.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. A bytecode scan of the application found JavaScriptUtils called only from the Spring JSP tag classes (EscapeBodyTag, EvalTag, MessageTag and UrlTag). The application bundles no JSP engine and renders no JSP views, and none of its own classes calls JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape(), so the faulty escaping never runs.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service attacks when resolving static resources. More precisely, an application can be vulnerable when all the following are true: the application is using Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux; the application is serving static resources from the file system; the application is running on a Windows platform. When all the conditions above are met, the attacker can send malicious requests that are slow to resolve and that can keep HTTP connections in use. This can cause a Denial of Service on the application.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component serves static resources from the file system.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which serves no static resources from the file system, and the Docker images run on Linux rather than the Windows platform the advisory requires.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0 and 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 7.0.7 or newer, which include the fix. The advisory needs the application to serve static resources from the file system and to run on Windows. The application packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources properties, and none of its own classes registers a resource handler, so it serves nothing from the file system; Spring Boot's default static locations are classpath locations only. The Docker images run on Linux. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths.

vulnerabilities.description: Use of XsltView in a Spring MVC application can result in SSRF and RCE attack if the application has an "/**" mapping that results in view rendering, and where the view name is not explicitly specified. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 - 7.0.8; 6.2.0 - 6.2.19; 6.1.0 - 6.1.28; 6.0.0 - 6.0.30; 5.3.0 - 5.3.49; 5.2.25.RELEASE and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component renders XsltView views or maps "/**" to view rendering.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which uses only REST controllers with explicit paths and never configures XsltView, so the vulnerable view-rendering path cannot be reached.

analysis.detail: The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Liquibase Secure Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); the Liquibase CLI itself contains no Spring MVC code. The application bundles spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, 7.0.7 in 5.2.0 and 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2, all in range. The advisory requires an application that renders views through XsltView, has a "/**" mapping that leads to view rendering, and leaves the view name implicit. A source review of the application found no XsltView, XsltViewResolver, ViewResolver or ModelAndView references, no .xsl resources, no spring.mvc.view properties and no "/**" mapping. All three of its controllers are @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths that return response bodies, never view names; its one HTML report is rendered by hand with mustache.java, not through a Spring view.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to stream corruption when using Server-Sent Events (SSE) with view fragments. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 - 7.0.8; 6.2.0 - 6.2.19.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component streams Server-Sent Events or renders view fragments.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which neither emits Server-Sent Events nor renders view fragments, so the vulnerable SSE fragment path is never executed.

analysis.detail: The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Liquibase Secure Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); the Liquibase CLI itself contains no Spring MVC code. The application bundles spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, 7.0.7 in 5.2.0 and 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2, all in range. The advisory requires an application that streams Server-Sent Events containing view fragments. A source review of the application found no SseEmitter, ServerSentEvent, text/event-stream, FragmentsRendering or WebFlux usage, and no Spring view rendering of any kind: its controllers are @RestController classes returning plain JSON, text or hand-rendered HTML bodies.

vulnerabilities.description: A Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux application which configures a mapping for "/**" where the view name is not explicitly specified allows an attacker to craft a link resulting in a 302 redirect to an arbitrary external host via the redirect: prefix. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component maps "/**" to view rendering.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which uses only REST controllers with explicit paths and never resolves view names from the request path.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory requires a "/**" mapping that resolves to view rendering without an explicit view name, so that the view name is derived from the request path and a "redirect:" prefix can be injected. A source and bytecode review of the application found no view controllers, ViewResolver, ModelAndView, WebMvcConfigurer or "/**" handler mapping of its own. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths that return response bodies, never view names.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC applications which accept user-supplied values in the cssClass, cssErrorClass, or cssStyle attributes of JSP form tags allow arbitrary HTML/JavaScript code injection, potentially resulting in a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component renders JSP pages.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which has no JSP engine and no JSP pages, so the vulnerable form tags never run.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The flaw is in the Spring JSP form tag library, which runs only when JSP pages are rendered. The application contains no JSP files or taglib declarations and does not bundle a JSP engine (tomcat-embed-jasper), so Spring form tags are never executed. Its one HTML report is rendered with mustache.java from a fixed template, not through Spring views.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Information Disclosure attacks when resolving static resources. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component protects static resources with authentication or enables the Spring resource chain cache.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which has no authentication, serves no static resources and does not enable the resource chain whose cache the advisory concerns.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory needs several resource handlers with different locations, at least one of which requires authentication, sharing one resource cache, so that a public resource resolved and cached first is served in place of a protected one with the same name. The application has no Spring Security or other authentication, so no resource is protected. It packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources properties, and none of its own classes registers a resource handler. Spring Boot's default resource handlers run without the resource chain and its cache, which Boot enables only when the resource-chain properties are set. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Path Traversal attacks when resolving static resources. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures versioned static resource support.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which does not configure the versioned static resource handling the advisory requires.

The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory needs static resources served from the file system with versioned resource support configured. The application serves nothing from the file system: it sets no spring.web.resources properties, so only Spring Boot's default classpath locations are mapped, and it packages no static resources there. None of its own classes references VersionResourceResolver, ResourceChainRegistration or a resource-handler registry, and Spring Boot registers versioned resource resolution only when the resource-chain strategy properties are set. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Multipart request smuggling attacks. Affected versions: Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.48 and earlier.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component accepts multipart requests.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, whose endpoints take JSON or no input and never read multipart content, so a smuggled multipart part reaches no handler.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0, 7.0.6 in 5.1.1 and 7.0.7 in 5.2.0, all in range, and the fixed 7.0.8 in 5.2.1 and 5.2.2. The advisory needs an application that accepts multipart requests and sits behind a web application firewall or proxy that parses multipart bodies and makes security decisions on their content, so that a request the firewall reads as harmless is parsed differently by Spring. Spring Boot registers its standard multipart resolver by default and the application does not turn it off, but no handler accepts multipart content. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes: v1/track takes a JSON @RequestBody, and v1/report and v1/health are GET methods without parameters. None of its classes references MultipartFile, @RequestPart, @RequestParam, a MultipartResolver or the servlet request, and it sets no spring.servlet.multipart properties. Liquibase ships no firewall or proxy in front of it.

vulnerabilities.description: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to cache poisoning when resolving static resources. More precisely, an application can be vulnerable when all the following are true: the application is using Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux; the application is configuring the resource chain support with caching enabled; the application adds support for encoded resources resolution; the resource cache must be empty when the attacker has access to the application. When all the conditions above are met, the attacker can send malicious requests and poison the resource cache with resources using the wrong encoding. This can cause a denial of service by breaking the front-end application for clients.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component enables the Spring resource chain cache or encoded resource resolution.

ratings.justification: Spring MVC ships only inside the 5.x license-tracking application, which serves no static resources and enables neither the resource chain cache nor encoded resource resolution that the advisory requires.

analysis.detail: The Liquibase CLI contains no Spring code. The scanner reports spring-webmvc from the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries spring-webmvc 6.2.2 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 6.2.12 in 5.0.3, 7.0.3 in 5.1.0 and 7.0.6 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 7.0.7 or newer, which include the fix. The advisory needs the application to configure the Spring resource chain with caching enabled and to add encoded resource resolution. The application packages no static resources, sets no spring.web.resources properties, and none of its own classes registers a resource handler or resource resolver. Spring Boot's default resource handlers run without the resource chain and its cache, which Boot enables only when the resource-chain properties are set. Its only controllers are three @RestController classes with explicit v1/track, v1/report and v1/health paths.
